memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Everyone who does any of these detestable things — such persons must be cut off from their people. Keep my requirements and do not follow any of the detestable customs that were practised before you came and do not defile yourselves with them. I am the LORD your God.'" - Lev 18:28-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends where it began: I am the LORD your God. The same words that opened it now close it. Everything difficult in between is held between those bookends.

And the final warning is against drift. Do not follow any of the detestable customs that were practised before you came.

Notice that word customs. Not laws forced on them — customs. The ordinary, unremarkable way things were done around them. Nobody was going to compel Israel to adopt Canaanite practices. They would simply be there, normal, everywhere, until one day they were normal in Israel too.

That is how God's people are usually lost. Not through dramatic rebellion but through gradual absorption. What was shocking becomes debatable. What was debatable becomes acceptable. What was acceptable becomes normal.

The New Testament calls us to stay alert to this. Be alert and of sober mind (1 Pet 5:8). Do not conform (Rom 12:2). See to it that no one takes you captive through hollow and deceptive philosophy (Col 2:8).

But end where the chapter ends. I am the LORD your God. He is not standing over you with a list. He is your God, who rescued you, who holds you, and who is worth living differently for.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you slowly absorbed something you would once have questioned?
2. What helps you stay alert to gradual drift?
3. How does "I am the LORD your God" change how you read this chapter?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are my God, and that everything You ask sits inside that relationship. Keep me from drifting, and hold me close to You. Amen.
